body:
Both amendments accepted as written, and amendment 1 caught me inside the hour.

ON AMENDMENT 1 — accepted, and I have a second instance for you, which is my own.

At 16:04 I posted a rework brief on BUG-1429 opening with "AC3 survived round 1, so this brief does not restate it." Then I read your mail and ran the check your precondition asks for. `gh api repos/joemooney/aida/pulls/2021/commits` returns exactly one commit, c84ce1c89. There was no round 1 to survive. This is the first verdict.

So within minutes of you handing me the precondition I had already violated it, in the very brief that was supposed to demonstrate the rule. I have posted a correction onto the spec rather than editing the framing away, because the false claim is the more instructive artifact.

What the two instances have in common is worth naming, because it is not what I would have guessed. Yours (STORY-1350) was a round that moved the head without moving the content. Mine was a round count I inferred from the verdict's word "still" rather than counting. Both are the same failure at different removes: treating a SURFACE SIGNAL of progress as evidence about the work. The head moved; the reviewer said "still". Neither is the branch's own contribution, and only the branch's own contribution is evidence.

That suggests the entry's precondition generalises slightly beyond patch-ids: **before drawing any conclusion from a repeated finding, count the rounds from the branch's commits, and compare the branch's own contribution across them.** The first clause catches my failure, the second catches yours. I would not go further than that — two cases is two cases.

ON AMENDMENT 2 — accepted without reservation, and the second family earned another member tonight.

"Instruments that cannot see themselves" is the right name and the scope fix is right. Add to your four:

  the portability ratchet, which exists specifically to catch Linux-only assumptions
  at PR time, and has no rule for the Linux-only assumption that has held the
  cross-platform nightly red for three nights.

Details below. It is a cleaner specimen than the four you listed because the instrument's charter and the miss are the same sentence.

ON THE LOST VERDICT ROUNDS. Your PR-2016 evidence is stronger than mine and it changes my read of STORY-1391's priority. I had it as preparatory work for a detection feature; you are right that it is load-bearing for a decision already made. A narrowing of acceptance whose entire justification was three rounds naming three different site-sets, where the three rounds no longer exist, is not auditable — and BUG-1310's narrowing is the kind of call that gets revisited precisely when someone doubts it. Raise it on that basis; I am not going to argue for the feature framing over the audit framing.

ACTION I NEED FROM YOU — BUG-1453, filed draft, needs approval.

I asked for `--status approved` and the authority seam correctly refused it, so it is sitting in your triage queue. Summary:

The cross-platform nightly has failed four consecutive runs. macOS green every time. Windows fails one assertion out of 5092 passing tests — `auto_bump_done_tests.rs:2080`, "PR closed without merging should reject the review spec, was Approved".

Not a product defect. TASK-1296's new test writes a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` fake `gh` to `<root>/gh` with a `#[cfg(unix)]` chmod. Windows cannot execute a shebang script via CreateProcess, so the forge lookup finds nothing and every seeded spec stays Approved. Sibling tests doing the same thing carry `#[cfg(unix)]` above `#[test]` — task_471_stale_base_preflight_tests.rs:104, story_429_auto_rebase_tests.rs:71. This one omitted the gate.

Why it is worth your attention rather than just a one-line fix: `scripts/pre-release-check.sh` blocks tagging on cross-platform green within 24h, so one ungated fixture currently blocks every release. The spec carries two halves — the gate, and a `shebang-fake-binary` rule for `portability-rules.json` so the ratchet fails PR CI on the next one. The second half is the durable part.

Caveat on verification, stated in the spec: the Windows leg cannot be confirmed locally. Whoever takes it must dispatch `gh workflow run cross-platform.yml --ref <branch>` and read the Windows job before calling it done. That makes it a poor unattended-drain candidate despite being a small diff, and you may want to route it accordingly.

ONE NON-BUG, so you do not chase it. Thirteen open PRs currently show `merge-hold-gate` twice in their check rollup, once SUCCESS and once FAILURE, which reads like a duplicated required check. It is not. On #2021 the SUCCESS is run 35520246009 at 15:39:07 (PR opened, no hold yet) and the FAILURE is run 35521409425 at 16:01:54 (after you applied the hold at 15:53). Two runs of the same check across a state change, latest wins, gate behaving correctly. I checked before filing.

STATE. Drain is active on batch night-0920, TASK-176 in phase 1, eight queued behind it. BUG-1429 was orphaned In-Progress with no live lease (`aida ps` said flag-only) so I reset it to approved for the next wave rather than force-claiming into this checkout. Twenty PRs open; the recent eleven are held on your review, which is where the throughput sits, and I am not going to pretend that is a problem I can solve by filing more.
